newsitem.title: PERU: Peru posts $75.2 mln trade surplus in June-customs.
newsitem.headline: Peru posts $75.2 mln trade surplus in June-customs.

text.p: The Customs Service said Thursday that for the first time in five years Peru posted a positive monthly trade balance, reporting a surplus of $75.2 million in June.
The June surplus meant the country's trade gap in the first half of the year fell 42.8 percent to $512.9 million, compared with the same period last year, the service said in statement.
In June, Peru exported goods worth $716.7 million and imported goods worth $641.5 million, the government body said, without giving comparative figures for 1996.
Exports were $3.422 billion in the first half of the year, up $562 million from the same period in 1996. The service did not publish import figures.
The Customs figures do not include all the data used to calculate the Central Reserve Bank's official trade balance figures, which are published later.
